title: Kernel Pathology Notebook: quantized edge-case triage and throughput/quality lexicon
content:
Status: draft - notebook-style working notes and reproducible snippets.

1) One-line summary
We saw a reproducible throughput collapse and quality cliff across several customer-like workloads when switching some layers to AWQ/GPTQ kernels on older Ampere cards. This doc records experiments, microprofiles, hypotheses, and mitigations that appear to restore stable throughput with minimal quality loss.

2) Motivation / why this matters- Customers run mixed workloads (short chat turns + occasional long context retrieval). We need kernel-selection heuristics that avoid severe tail latency/throughput regressions while preserving quantization unit-cost gains. Current perf regressions show up only on specific layer-shapes + sequence-length distributions and are hard to catch in synthetic sweeps.

3) Observed symptoms (field and lab)- Host: g4dn-like (A10G), older drivers, CUDA 12.3- Models: 7B-family open model, 70B trimmed eval set- Quant configs: per-channel AWQ for attention, GPTQ for feedforward, int8 for output projection, occasional fp8 for head layers- Symptom timeline: after warmup throughput looks fine, then at 30–120s throughput drops 40–70% and latency tail spikes; token-quality (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-sim) degrades slightly on some prompts; logs show repeated kernel fallsbacks and memcpy storms.

4) Quick reproduction (local harness)- Command (client-sim): 
  ./client_sim --model modelA --quant awq+gptq --seq-dist mixed --concurrency 48 --sim-duration 300 --kv-cache on

Add environment variables: 
  RUNTIME_DEBUG_KERNELS=1 RUNTIME_PROFILE_MS=10 RUNTIME_SWAP_THRESHOLD=0.6

Reproduces in ~2 runs out of 5 (non-deterministic timing).

5) Microprofiling snapshot (representative run)
- Total token throughput: 0.62 tokens/ms (degraded run) vs 1.58 tokens/ms (baseline)
- Time breakdown (percent of active compute time):
  - matmul kernels (attention): 46%
  - matmul kernels (FFN): 22%
  - memcpy/host-device: 18%
  - kernel scheduling / queuing: 9%
  - other (softmax, layernorm): 5%
- Observed anomalies: 
  - memcpy spikes coincide with kernel-switch events in logs (we saw ~6 kernel-switches/min).
  - Attention matmul splits between two kernel variants (vec-lane-fast and compact-block). The compact-block variant has 20% worse throughput but dominates for certain sequence lengths.

6) Hypotheses (ranked)
A) Kernel-switchover jitter: small timing shifts cause the scheduler to pick compact-block repeatedly which creates fragmentation and extra memcopies when buffers are reallocated.
B) KV-cache alignment mismatch: AWQ per-channel packing uses a different alignment that triggers suboptimal memory paths on these cards leading to cache-line inefficiencies.
C) Interference between AWQ packing and GPUDirect paths: when the transfer size crosses a threshold we lose peer-copy and fall back to staging, increasing memcpy percent.
D) Layer-wise precision sensitivity: some feedforward layers in this model are extremely sensitive to int8/GPTQ for activations, causing more redo/retries in upper stacks that manifest as quality regressions.

7) Experiments run (configs and short notes)- E1: pin kernels to "vec-lane-fast" only (force selection)  - Result: baseline throughput restored (1.5 tokens/ms) but small quality dip on a subset of prompts.- E2: increase runtime stable-window to 200ms (prevent frequent switchover)  - Result: throughput improved 30% over degraded but still 10% below baseline; memcpys decreased.- E3: change AWQ packing alignment to 64B (was 128B)  - Result: removes memcpy cliff on A10G but not on A100; suggests HW-dependent alignment behavior.- E4: pin last two FFN layers to fp8 (mixed-precision fallback)  - Result: restores quality metrics for sensitive prompts with <5% throughput cost.- E5: run under isolated NIC path (disable GPUDirect)  - Result: memcpy% increased but jitter reduced — suggests a race in GPUDirect path.

8) Representative logs (abbreviated)
[2026-12-04T12:03:21.431Z] kernel-switch: layer=attn_12 old=vec-lane-fast new=compact-block reason=throughput-estimation[2026-12-04T12:03:21.560Z] memcpy: staging-buffer allocate 24MB[2026-12-04T12:03:22.112Z] kernel-submit: compact-block (lat=3.1ms)[2026-12-04T12:03:22.116Z] kernel-switch: layer=attn_12 old=compact-block new=vec-lane-fast reason=latency-estimation

9) Quality checks (mini-eval)- Short-chat prompts (n=100): semantic-sim drop from 0.84 to 0.81 in degraded runs- Long-context summarization (n=30): ROUGE-L drop of 1.7 points when FFN quantized to int8 for two specific layers

10) Actionable mitigations (short term)- 10.1 Per-layer precision pinning: mark top-k sensitivity layers to fp8 or float during model onboarding (configurable). We prototyped heuristics to auto-detect these using a 200-prompt quality probe.- 10.2 Stabilize kernel selection: increase the selection hysteresis window (eg from 50ms -> 200ms) and add a min-run threshold (e.g., kernel must be estimated to be >10k tokens of expected benefit).- 10.3 Avoid alignment penalty on Ampere gen: add a runtime packer that chooses 64B or 128B alignment based on detected card and driver; fallback to 64B for A10G.- 10.4 GPUDirect race mitigation: add a short backoff before switching staging strategy when a peer-copy fails; this reduced memcpy storm in E5.

11) Longer-term follow-ups- L1: Gather kernel-run-length histograms in production (probe for quick-flip pattern) and create an alert when average run-length < 3s for any hot layer. (JIRA-ENG-3198)- L2: Add microbench harness for mixed seq distributions (short-heavy + occasional long) to CI so we catch these triage patterns.- L3: Investigate a "sticky kernel" policy that favors the currently-running kernel unless an expected throughput delta > X% for at least Y tokens.- L4: Measurement: build a per-layerESS (estimated service seconds) metric that combines exec-time + memcpy overhead for decision making.

12) Data artifacts and how to re-run experiments- Harness: runtime/tools/client_sim (branch: kernel-pathology/experiment)- Repro commands: see section 4. Use --seed to make deterministic.- Perf traces: s3://redwood-qa/quant-pathology/dec2026/run-*/trace.json (access via internal creds)

13) Open questions / notes to self- Why do older Ampere cards prefer 64B pack? Need to consult NV driver docs and maybe test on different driver stacks.- The noise in switchover decisions suggests our throughput model is overly reactive to micro-variation; a Bayesian smoothing might help.- Check whether the same pathology shows up on Dedicated clusters (reserved pools) vs Hosted pods (noisy neighbors).

14) Short TODO list (owner in parens)- Add kernel run-length histograms to runtime telemetry (Priya).- Prototype sticky-kernel policy in sim harness (Marcus).- Add sensitivity probe to onboarding (Lina).- Write ticket to infra to test GPUDirect race on A10G/A100 combos (Ethan).

Appendix A - Quick sensitivity probe pseudocode- for layer in top_k_layers:
    for quant in [int8, gptq, awq, fp8]:
        run small eval (n=200)
        record quality metric
    select quant that respects quality threshold and minimizes cost

Appendix B - small ASCII table sample (run summary)
| config               | throughput (tokens/ms) | memcpy % | quality delta |
|----------------------|------------------------|----------|---------------|
| baseline fp32        | 1.58                   | 6%       | 0.00          |
| awq+gptq (auto)      | 0.62                   | 18%      | -0.03         |
| awq+gptq (sticky=200)| 1.02                   | 9%       | -0.02         |
| awq+gptq (pin-last2) | 1.45                   | 8%       | -0.01         |
